G.reason: Genuine practitioner gap with broad related work, but it is an integration/usability gap; no evidence that fragmentation limits results, no platform-level neighbor (e.g. DSPy-style toolkits) comparison.

M.reason: The method is a layered architecture that wraps existing algorithms; the generic operator equations add no mechanism, workflow generation is not described, and the memory optimizer is unimplemented, so the problem-to-operation reasoning is thin.

X.reason: Layers and class interfaces are shown with code, but selection, acceptance, rollback and versioning policy of evolved artifacts are inherited or absent; the evaluation protocol that makes the loop reconstructable is missing.

E.measurement.reason: Ground-truth metrics (F1, pass@1, solve rate, GAIA accuracy) are credible, but sample sizes, models, splits and the optimizer selected per benchmark are unreported, and GAIA numbers are given only as percentage changes.

E.causality.reason: Original-vs-optimized comparison exists, but no direct-run reference implementations, no alternative optimizers or random-edit baseline, no compute-matched control, and one optimizer lowers a score contradicting "consistent".

E.holdout.reason: No statement of optimization vs evaluation split; Table 1 lists no dev/train for MBPP and no test for HotPotQA; best-of-three optimizer chosen per benchmark.

E.statistics.reason: Single numbers per cell; no sample counts, seeds, repeats or intervals.

E.cost.reason: No optimization rounds, tokens, calls, dollars or wall-clock for any reported experiment; only an example config.

rationale: Demo-style platform paper wrapping TextGrad, AFlow and MIPRO; benchmark gains come from the integrated algorithms with unreported splits, variance and cost, and one optimizer reduces accuracy, so evidence for the platform claim is thin.
